# The Keepers of the Light: Lighthouse Staffing and Maintenance in the Nineteenth Century

## A Life of Quiet Vigilance

There is a particular quality to the work of a lighthouse keeper in the 1800s that resists easy romanticization. It was not, for most of those who held the position, a life of thrilling adventure against the sea. It was a life of repetition, of small duties performed with care, of long stretches of solitude punctuated by the occasional arrival of a supply boat or the rare visit from a district inspector. The work was essential, and it was, in its own quiet way, a kind of devotion.

## The Keepers Themselves

In the United States, lighthouse keepers were appointed by the federal government through the Lighthouse Establishment, which operated under the Treasury Department until 1852, when it was reorganized into the U.S. Lighthouse Board
